title: Inverse trigonometric ranges and an expression rewritten as a single tangent
intro: No calculator. Give exact values, use radians, and show the work for each part. Only real solutions are asked for.

parts.label: A(i)

rubric.point: $-\frac{\pi}{3}$ (an angle outside $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ such as $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ earns no point)

parts.sample: $\tan^{-1}$ returns the angle in $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ with the given tangent. $\tan\frac{\pi}{3} = \sqrt{3}$ and tangent is odd, so $\tan^{-1}\left(-\sqrt{3}\right) = -\frac{\pi}{3}$.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.sample: $\sin\frac{5\pi}{4} = -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$. The angle in $\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]$ with that sine is $-\frac{\pi}{4}$, so the value is $-\frac{\pi}{4}$ (not $\frac{5\pi}{4}$).

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Rewrite $h(x) = \frac{\sin(2x)}{1 + \cos(2x)}$ as a single trigonometric function of $x$. Show the identities you use.

rubric.point: Uses $\sin(2x) = 2\sin x\cos x$ and $1 + \cos(2x) = 2\cos^2 x$ (from $\cos(2x) = 2\cos^2 x - 1$)
$h(x) = \tan x$ as one function (stopping at $\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ earns no point)

parts.sample: $\sin(2x) = 2\sin x\cos x$ and $1 + \cos(2x) = 1 + (2\cos^2 x - 1) = 2\cos^2 x$. So $h(x) = \frac{2\sin x\cos x}{2\cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos x} = \tan x$.

parts.label: C

rubric.point: Uses part B to write $\tan x = \sqrt{3}$ and gives one correct solution
Both solutions $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and $x = \frac{4\pi}{3}$, and no others

parts.sample: By part B, $\tan x = \sqrt{3}$. The principal value is $\frac{\pi}{3}$; tangent has period $\pi$, so $\frac{4\pi}{3}$ also works. At both, $1 + \cos(2x) = \frac{1}{2} \ne 0$, so $h$ is defined. The solutions are $x = \frac{\pi}{3}$ and $x = \frac{4\pi}{3}$.
